# DSH Intelligent Router
> Intelligent LLM routing for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) — Multi-model Routing Strategies, Automatic Fai
lover, Cache-affinity Staying, Data Anonymization and a Visual Settings UI.
The router registers itself as the **`auto`** provider in DSH. Pick **AUTO – Intelligent Router** as
your model and every request is routed to the best member of your configured route group — with rul
es, strategies, failover, and prompt-cache-aware staying working under the hood.
## Architecture
> DSH Intelligent Router registers as the `auto` provider in DeepSeek Harness and routes each reques
t through configurable route groups, strategies, intent rules, cache-affinity Stays, and automatic f
h configurable route groups, strategies, intent rules, cache-affinity Stays, and automatic failover.
## Usage demo
The screenshot below shows a real DSH chat flow with `AUTO - Intelligent Router`: the request is cla
ssified, matched against routing rules, and served by the selected provider/model member.

## Features

### Routing
- **Route groups** — organize members (provider + model) and manage them from the Settin

gs UI
- **Four routing strategies** — `order` (priority) · `smart` (task-size aware: local vs cloud)

· `rotate` (round-robin) · `usage` (least-used first)
- **Rule engine** — `minTokens` / `hasImage`
/ `anyAgent` / `intent` conditions; the first matching rule pins its target model to the front of th

e candidate chain
- **Intent routing** — a lightweight classifier model (your choice) labels the mes

sage intent; rules route on it
- **Stays (cache affinity)** — `off` / `turn` / `auto` / `session` (d
efault `session`): keeps the last successful member at the front while the vendor prompt cache is wo
rth keeping, keyed per DSH session

### Reliability
- **Automatic failover** — three-tier error classification (TRANSIENT / PERMANENT /
UNKNOWN), no false positives: auth and validation errors never burn retries; connection, rate-limit,

and 5xx errors fall through to the next candidate
- **Quota guard** — members that exceed limits ar
e skipped without consuming a retry

### Experience
- **Settings UI** (Magpie-style, zh/en) — model picker fed from DSH's configured mode
ls, strategy pills, rule builder, intent-classifier selection, save-time validation, live persistenc

e via the DSH settings service
- **Observability** — per-group/per-member metrics, latency tracking,
cost estimates, and `router/fallback` events (host side)
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.0-rc.2` (declared in `compatibility.json`)
- Node.js `>= 18` (DSH runtime
), pnpm for development

> [!WARNING]
> **First-time install requires a DSH restart.** The plugin's loader entry and client b

undle are composed into the boot graph **at server startup**.
> If DSH is already running when you i
nstall, it will not notice the new package — the Settings UI (and the `auto` provider) will be missi

ng until you restart.
> Stop the running `dsh web` process and start it again; a browser reload alon
e is not enough. Subsequent changes to routing config (Save in the Settings UI) or rebuilt plugin bu

ndles are picked up live via HMR — only package-level install/remove needs a restart.
> **Waiting fo
r DSH support in the future.**
> Start DSH from the profile directory with the **local binary** (`cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web && ./node_
modules/.bin/dsh web --port 3082`). Launching via `npx` can load a duplicate module tree and break s
h web --port 3082`). Launching via `npx` can load a duplicate module tree and break settings writes.
## Quick Start

1. Start DSH and open **Settings → Built-in plugins → LLM Router**
2. Click **+ Add model** to pick

members from your DSH-configured providers
3. Choose a strategy (default: `order`); optionally add r

ules
4. Click **Save** (persists immediately via the DSH settings service)
5. In chat, select **AUTO
– Intelligent Router** — done
Use a specific group with provider `group/<groupId>`.

host afterwards (boot → restart → Settings UI bundle contract → doctor).
## Roadmap
- `pace` / `weighted` / `intent` strategies are declared in the schema but **not implemented** (they

silently degrade to `order`) — implement or prune
- Stays windows (`turn` ≈ 2 min, `auto` ≈ 5 min)

are hardcoded approximations — make configurable
- Quota limits are hardcoded (1M tokens/day, 1k req

uests/day) and never auto-reset — wire up `quotaTracking.limits`
- Monitoring data has no UI channel

yet (panel shows mock data)
- Middleware system is implemented but not wired into the request path
- Prune the legacy dual call path (`route()` waterfall / `llm-client.ts`)
